findings.title: Size restored windows using their actual screen
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the uncapped 1600x1100 target into InitialWindowFrame and clamp it using window.screen?.visibleFrame inside viewDidMoveToWindow; keep defaultSize separately capped for initial scene creation if needed.
findings.first_evidence: msgblast/App/msgblastApp.swift:11 -- let screen = NSScreen.main?.visibleFrame.size ?? NSSize(width: 1600, height: 1100)
findings.why_it_matters: A window restored on a larger external display can open substantially smaller than the requested 1600x1100 size when the main display is a smaller laptop screen. The preferred size is capped against NSScreen.main before the window exists, and the later frame adjustment can only reduce that size. Compute the 1600x1100 target against the window's screen when applying its frame so each launch window uses its own visible area.

msgblast/App/msgblastApp.swift:12 -- return NSSize(width: min(1600, screen.width), height: min(1100, screen.height))
msgblast/App/msgblastApp.swift:21 -- }.background(InitialWindowFrame(size: initialWindowSize))
msgblast/App/msgblastApp.swift:99 -- guard let window, let screen = window.screen ?? NSScreen.main else { return }
msgblast/App/msgblastApp.swift:101 -- let width = min(size.width, bounds.width), height = min(size.height, bounds.height)
Apple NSScreen.main documentation: identifies the display of the keyboard-focused window, not necessarily the newly restored window; https://developer.apple.com/documentation/AppKit/NSScreen/main
findings.validation_reason: When the screen used during scene construction is smaller than the restored window's screen, msgblast/App/msgblastApp.swift:11-12 caps the target prematurely, lines 83-87 retain that capped size, and lines 99-103 can only reduce it further; [Apple's NSScreen.main contract](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/AppKit/NSScreen/main) permits that display mismatch, so a two-display restoration test would expose this newly introduced sizing defect, although incidence was not measured.

findings.title: Preserve storage failures across navigation recovery
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the persistent storage diagnostic when storageFailed is true: prevent failedNavigation and the blocked-link policy callback from replacing it with navigationError, or store the persistent diagnostic separately and restore it in didFinish. Extend testSuccessfulPageLoadClearsOnlyNavigationErrors with the existing broken-storage session receiving a non-cancelled navigation failure before its successful load; the storage warning must remain afterward.
findings.first_evidence: msgblast/Core/WebAgentSession.swift:343 -- if let navigationError, error == navigationError { error = nil }
findings.why_it_matters: A session with unreadable or unwritable storage can lose its repair warning after a network failure followed by a successful reload, even though storageFailed remains true and sending is still blocked. The navigation failure overwrites the storage message, and this new success path then clears the replacement to nil; comparing the current message with navigationError cannot recover the displaced persistent failure. Keep the storage error visible when recording transient navigation errors, or retain it separately and restore it after recovery.
